bio.summary: Richmond is a first-time council candidate and a diversity and education consultant. She advocates community-led governance, affordable housing and support for workers and small businesses.

statements.text: The DDA vote tells us something real about where this city is right now.
statements.speaker: Jamillah Richmond

statements.text: I support the reconsideration of the DDA, it was not a plan without creativity, it was a plan that lacked community engagement, transparency and buy in.
statements.speaker: Jamillah Richmond
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Jamillah Richmond

statements.text: Her priorities also included affordable childcare and living wages.
statements.speaker: Peter Constas (reporting the candidate)

statements.text: This city seems to always be debating land, taxes and affordability.
statements.speaker: Jamillah Richmond

statements.text: As the co-founder of a non-profit in Boulder, and previous owner of a for profit business and single parent with a job it is important to me that there is meaningful engagement between sectors, that allow for business owners and employees alike to have a voice.
statements.speaker: Jamillah Richmond
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Jamillah Richmond

statements.text: One of the reasons I am running is to bring more community-driven governance to how we operate as a city.
statements.speaker: Jamillah Richmond

statements.text: Jamillah Richmond is a first-time candidate for Boulder City Council running on a platform of climate justice, community-driven government, affordable housing and supporting workers and small businesses.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter

statements.text: I think all community members should expect to feel safe from harm and that they can rely on city governance to help support that.
statements.speaker: Jamillah Richmond
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Jamillah Richmond

forum_quotes.question: If elected, name your top three priorities. And do you believe the city is moving in the right direction or wrong direction on those top priorities?
forum_quotes.quote: I am a single parent that lives in affordable housing. And so my first priority would be housing. Housing that is accessible to the lowest wages of us and our middle income earners.
